slice: India bets on cheaper AI and fuel. The world’s lesson: what you show, ship or see can be taken.

callouts.text: LIC forms being digitised with custom AI models, says Sarvam’s Pratyush Kumar.
China-to-Iran shipments with dual-use parts for Iran’s defence ministry, January to June.

stories.title: Sarvam: India will be AI’s biggest user in five years
points: Co-founder Pratyush Kumar calls this “year one for India AI”.
He says India should speed up how it builds and adopts AI.
The catch: the cost of using AI has to keep falling.
stories.why: Scale is India’s edge; price sets the pace.

stories.title: Govt weighs a ₹20,000 cr fund for frontier AI
points: Proposed ₹15,000–20,000 cr anchor under the IndiaAI Mission.
Would back AI startups, GPU clusters and data centres.
Could be set up as a SEBI-regulated Category I AIF.
stories.why: The state wants to be AI’s anchor investor.

stories.title: Gadkari: a pure-ethanol car at ‘₹25 a litre’
points: Toyota’s 100% ethanol Innova launches in October, he says.
Claims running cost equals petrol at about ₹25 a litre.
No complaints so far on ethanol-blended fuel, he adds.
stories.why: A minister’s claim; the proof is at the pump.

stories.title: YouTuber flaunts gold online; burglars strike
points: Nagercoil home broken into while the family was out, Sept 24.
Thieves forced the back door and took gold kept in a bureau.
Police are checking the videos; no link confirmed yet.
stories.why: Your reel can be a burglar’s recce.

stories.title: The ‘India shock’: exporting workers, not goods
points: About 1mn join the workforce each month; too few good jobs, so talent heads abroad.
Backlash abroad is rising, and brain drain may cost $35–50bn a year.
stories.why: Remittances ease the strain; only jobs at home solve it.

stories.title: Iran’s secret weapon against America: China
points: As Beijing hailed its role in a US–Iran truce, a Chinese plane landed in Tehran.
China is now the only major buyer of Iranian oil.
Chinese front companies and banks help move the money.
stories.why: Peacemaker in public, supplier in private.

stories.title: F-35 parts bound for US repair end up in Hong Kong
points: Sent from Australia for US repairs, it went to Hong Kong.
Australia is investigating how the parts went missing.
stories.why: A stealth jet is only as secure as its courier.

stories.title: Meta doubles down despite the ‘pervert glasses’ jibe
points: Videos of men secretly filming women sparked the backlash.
Meta now disables the camera if the LED is tampered with.
Snap, Google and Samsung are pushing their own AI glasses.
stories.why: Stigma hasn’t stopped sales; trust is next.
